title: Noninvasive Measurements of Renal Perfusion During Cardiac Surgery
brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to assess the feasibility of measuring urine oxygen tension in cardiac surgery patient and the ability of peri-operative urine oxygen measurements to predict post-operative acute kidney injury. The hypothesis is that a small oxymeter placed in a urinary catheter will provide reliable measurement of urine oxygenation and that these measurements will predict post-operative acute kidney injury in cardiac surgery patients.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Elective or semi-elective/urgent Cardiac surgery patients in whom CPB is a planned part of the procedure.
* 18 years or older
* Urinary catheter is planned during the surgery

Exclusion Criteria:

* Contra-indications to urinary catheter
* Pre-operative dialysis dependent end stage renal disease
* Emergency cases
study_population: Elective or semi-elective/urgent Cardiac surgery patients aged 18 and older in whom CPB is a planned part of the procedure and a urinary catheter is planned during the surgery will be enrolled. Patients with contra-indications to urinary catheter or pre-operative dialysis dependent end stage renal disease, and emergency cases will be excluded.
